problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $(x-2)^{2}=12(y+1)?$
worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =4(3)(y+1).\end{aligned}
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=3.$

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=2$ and $k=-1.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(2,-1).$
